name: Question 18
problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -6\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=-15 \\ 3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=30.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & -15 \\ 3 & -6 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 3 & -6 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 15\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 20 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}20 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}20 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 80 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the basis B of R2 (shown above) and a basis C of R3. The matrix [T]B|C of the linear map T:R2→R3 relative to these bases, and the vector x∈R2, are also given. Find [T(x)]C.

EXPLANATION

We can find the coordinates of the image of x under T relative to the basis C as follows:

[T(x)]C=[T]B|C⋅[x]B

First, we need to find [x]B, the coordinates of x relative to B. So, let

x=[−1530]=x1[−33]+x2[9−6].

This gives us the system {−3x1+9x2=−153x1−6x2=30.

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[−39−153−630]R1:=(−13)R1∼[1−353−630]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[1−350315]R2:=13R2∼[1−35015]R1:=R1+3R2∼[1020015]

Therefore, [x]B=[205].

Finally, we obtain

[T(x)]C=[T]B|C⋅[x]B=[2−540−13][205]=[1580−5].
